guides.purpose: Formula Foundry typing CORE A — the legal-move generator. Reads the typed formula-bank cards, classifies each card's input/output UNITS into a deterministic closed-set dimension, and decides whether one formula's output may legally feed another's input. Rejects dimensionally-incoherent compositions (bits→length, probability into an energy slot) — the silent-garbage hole the engine exists to close.

exports.name: classifyDimension
exports.outputs: { dimension, witness } — closed-set dimension + the matched witness token (or null)

exports.name: dimensionsCompatible
exports.outputs: { compatible, confidence, reason }

exports.name: catalogFormulas
exports.outputs: { cards, count, banks, skipped } — unified read-view over the typed formula-banks; corrupt banks are listed in skipped

exports.name: coverageReport
exports.outputs: { boundCount, kernelExportCount, unboundPrimitives, orphanCards, cardCount } — the kernel-fn↔bank-card binding worklist

exports.name: composeCheck
exports.outputs: { legal, compatibleSlots, reasons, from, to, outputDim } — whether A's output may legally feed B

exports.name: composableTargets
exports.outputs: array of legal downstream targets { to, slots, outputDim }

exports.name: composeOperatorSequences
exports.inputs: optional catalog + { min/max chain length, branching, domain filters }
exports.outputs: { sequences, count, truncated, truncation, params } — enumerated legal operator chains

exports.name: synthesizeFormulaCandidates
exports.outputs: { candidates, count, truncated } — research-status candidates

exports.name: draftFormulaBankCard
exports.outputs: a research-status bank card (promotionStatus:'research', advisoryOnly:true, implementedBy:null)

exports.name: proofPreflightCandidate
exports.outputs: { inert, hasBinding, reason, promotionStatus, advisoryOnly, validationOk, validationErrors }

guides.securityBoundary: READ-ONLY over the formula-bank files; mints NO production cards. Synthesis output is INERT — promotionStatus:'research', advisoryOnly:true, no kernel binding — and cannot promote until someone binds a real kernel symbol AND a green worked example clears math-proof-gate (Core B). No protected-path access. Deterministic: no RNG, no clock, sorted iteration, closed-set classification.
guides.whenToUse: Auditing math coverage (which kernel primitives are unbound / which cards are orphaned), checking whether two formulas can legally compose, enumerating legal operator chains, or prototyping new formula candidates by dimensional rules. The upstream typing gate before math-proof-gate validates.
gotchas: Dimension classification is keyword-based over a CLOSED set; short tokens (≤5 chars) require full word boundaries to avoid collisions with ordinary English (F-1 hardening).
UNKNOWN dimensions are treated as compatible-by-default (cannot be disproven) — an UNKNOWN slot is not a rejection.
Synthesized candidates are INERT and advisory; they NEVER auto-promote — binding + proof-gate is a separate manual step.
Corrupt bank files are silently skipped; the only visibility of lost cards is the `skipped` field of catalogFormulas.
Generator (synthesize) and scorer (bakeoff) are deliberately separate modules — this core does not grade its own candidates.

guides.purpose: Foundry CHUNK 3 — the bakeoff harness + the promotion/demotion ledger (the SCORER + GOVERNANCE side of Core B). Takes already-synthesized candidates as INPUT and runs them up a staged promotion ladder, recording every gate verdict to an append-only ledger. Deliberately the GENERATOR≠SCORER boundary: it never imports the synthesizer, so a synthesizer can never grade its own candidate.

exports.name: stableHash
exports.outputs: a deterministic stable hash string (sorted-key, no clock)

exports.name: PROMOTION_LADDER
exports.outputs: the ordered, frozen list of promotion rungs

exports.name: readLedger
exports.outputs: array of gate records (malformed lines skipped)

exports.name: appendGateRecord
exports.outputs: appends one JSONL line to the ledger (mkdir-safe)

exports.name: canPromote
exports.inputs: formula id + target rung + optional ledger
exports.outputs: boolean — whether the ladder + evidence permit promotion to that rung

exports.name: promote
exports.outputs: the promotion result; records a gate entry

exports.name: demote
exports.outputs: the demotion result; records a gate entry with the reason

exports.name: stage0Intake
exports.outputs: stage-0 intake verdict

exports.name: stage1Fixtures
exports.outputs: stage-1 fixture-test verdict

exports.name: stage2Counterexamples
exports.outputs: stage-2 counterexample-search verdict

exports.name: stage3RealData
exports.outputs: stage-3 real-data verdict with ACTUAL corpus totals (no top-N laundering) or a refusal

exports.name: runBakeoff
exports.outputs: the full staged bakeoff result

guides.securityBoundary: MUTATING but bounded: appends to the promotion/demotion LEDGER (_SYSTEM/state, append-only JSONL, mkdir-safe) — never deletes or rewrites. No protected-path access. DOMAIN-BLIND: nothing inspects a candidate's source domains to loosen/tighten a gate — music, frequency, magnetism, numerology, alchemy, information-theory clear the SAME rungs on the SAME evidence bar; a candidate fails only for insufficient evidence. Deterministic: no Math.random, no Date.now (timestamps via opts.stamp).
guides.whenToUse: Promoting/demoting a formula candidate through the evidence ladder, reading the gate-decision history, or running the full staged bakeoff over a candidate set. The governance/scoring counterpart to formula-foundry's generation.
gotchas: GENERATOR≠SCORER: this module never imports synthesizeFormulaCandidates — keep that separation; do not wire the synthesizer in.
Determinism requires the caller to pass opts.stamp — there is no clock inside; a missing stamp loses reproducibility.
stage3RealData reports REAL corpus totals or REFUSES — it will not emit a top-N severity-laundered count.
The ledger is append-only; a later record for an id supersedes earlier ones (read reconstructs current state).

guides.purpose: The OpenProcess Sum Pool — mathematical memory for started-but-unclosed work. Users + lanes start tasks/research/ideas/todos/skills/bugs/experiments/handoffs over days; many stay open and fall out of working memory. This ranks them by OPEN MASS (status + staleness hazard-decay + dependency centrality + risk + value) so 'what did we start but not finish?' gets a math-grounded answer, not a memory vibe. UI-agnostic and YURI-native (same across all lanes).

exports.name: OPEN_PROCESS_TYPES
exports.outputs: ['task','research','idea','todo','skill','bug','experiment','handoff']

exports.name: OPEN_PROCESS_STATES
exports.outputs: ['open','active','blocked','stale','closed']

exports.name: DEFAULT_WEIGHTS
exports.outputs: the default OpenMass term weights (status/age/dep/risk/value)

exports.name: staleness
exports.outputs: a hazard-decay staleness score (stale-but-open rises back into attention)

exports.name: openMass
exports.outputs: the scalar OpenMass for that process

exports.name: rankPool
exports.outputs: processes ranked by descending OpenMass

exports.name: poolTotal
exports.outputs: the summed OpenMass over the pool

exports.name: categoryPools
exports.outputs: OpenMass grouped/summed by category

exports.name: whatIsUnfinished
exports.outputs: the top-N highest-mass open processes with their next candidate action

exports.name: navigateCentrality
exports.outputs: dependency centrality per process via yuri-navigate.aggregateProcessCentrality

guides.securityBoundary: Pure / read-only ranking math — computes OpenMass over process objects supplied by the caller; persists nothing itself. navigateCentrality reads the canonical graph via yuri-navigate (also read-only). No protected-path access. Deterministic (sorted, hazard-decay, no RNG).
guides.whenToUse: Answering 'what did we start but not finish?', ranking open work by mass, summing pool/category load, or weighting a process by its dependency centrality. The math layer under the nervous system's afferent digest (yuri-nerve calls whatIsUnfinished).
gotchas: Staleness uses hazard-decay: a stale-but-open item RISES back in rank over time — it is not penalized into invisibility.
navigateCentrality is async and depends on yuri-navigate over the canonical graph; a stale graph yields stale centrality.
The pool is data-in/score-out — it does not own storage; the caller supplies the process objects (e.g. from the nerve store).

guides.purpose: Human-readable cockpit over the Originator lane-telemetry stream. JSONL is the audit substrate, not the operator experience: this reads originator-telemetry.jsonl, groups by traceId, COLLAPSES the noisy stream/stderr/stdout chunk events into counts, and prints a compact per-run timeline (start → model call → verification → exit) with elapsed, heartbeat count, chars streamed, and status — so the operator sees what a lane is doing without reading raw JSON.

exports.name: readTelemetry
exports.outputs: parsed telemetry events (malformed lines tolerated)

exports.name: summarizeByTrace
exports.outputs: per-traceId summary collapsing chunk events into counts (elapsed, heartbeats, chars, status)

exports.name: renderCockpit
exports.outputs: the compact human-readable cockpit string

guides.securityBoundary: Strictly READ-ONLY — reads the telemetry JSONL and renders it; never mutates telemetry. Input line-count is bounded (limit guard). No protected-path access.
guides.whenToUse: Inspecting what a dispatched lane run actually did (timeline, model call, verification, exit) without parsing raw originator-telemetry JSON; triaging a slow/failed lane run.
gotchas: It collapses stream/stderr/stdout chunk events into COUNTS — individual chunk payloads are not shown (by design, to stay compact).
Grouping is by traceId; a run without a stable traceId will not group cleanly.
Read-only over a live-appended file — a snapshot reflects the moment it was read.

guides.purpose: Gates a lane claim against its WorkSubstrate scope + discovery footprint BEFORE the energy gate runs. The energy gate scores a transition's quality; this is the upstream filter asking 'did the lane stay inside the authority it was granted, and how precise was its discovery?'. Rides on yuri-id-bridge (isProtectedPath/normalizePath — the protected veto) and yuri-navigate (impact centrality — the claim's blast radius).

exports.name: discoveryPrecisionGate
exports.inputs: a claim { targets, scope (allowed/denied), discovery records }
exports.outputs: { verdict, vetoes, precision, footprint, advisory_only } — a hard protected/scope veto blocks; precision is reported

exports.name: withNavigate
exports.outputs: the gate verdict enriched with yuri-navigate impact centrality (blast radius of the claim's graph targets)

guides.securityBoundary: ADVISORY pre-filter with a HARD veto: a protected-path or out-of-scope target produces a blocking veto (fail-closed via isProtectedPath, which is traversal-hardened so '../'-escapes are caught). Precision + impact are advisory_only (reported for the downstream energy/proof gates + operator). Reads the graph via yuri-navigate; writes nothing. Deterministic (sorted, no RNG/clock).
guides.whenToUse: Before accepting a lane's claim/transition — to confirm it stayed inside granted authority (scope + protected paths) and to surface how precise/wide-blast its discovery was, upstream of the energy gate.
gotchas: The verdict is ADVISORY except the protected/scope VETO, which is a hard block — do not treat the precision score as a gate by itself.
Protected-path detection is realpath/traversal-hardened (yuri-id-bridge), not lexical — '../' escapes are caught.
withNavigate is async (graph impact lookup); high impact_centrality means 'surface for review', not automatic block.

guides.purpose: Deterministic, READ-ONLY placement assessor for YURI artifacts. As YURI grows, generated artifacts (research docs, /tmp scratch, memories, reports, lane outputs, telemetry) land in pools that aren't clean enough. This is the ASSESSMENT half of the filing system: classify an artifact → its canonical zone, score purge candidates by hazard-decay staleness, and dedup. It RECOMMENDS; it never moves or deletes a file.

exports.name: ZONE_RULES
exports.outputs: the closed-set ordered rules mapping a path → its canonical zone

exports.name: classifyArtifact
exports.outputs: the canonical zone the artifact belongs in (closed-set)

exports.name: assess
exports.outputs: { zone, current, misfiled, staleness, recommendation, advisory_only } — protected paths are vetoed (never recommended for move/purge)

exports.name: stalenessScore
exports.outputs: a hazard-decay staleness score (math-kernel confidenceDecay)

exports.name: assessAll
exports.outputs: a sorted assessment report over all paths

guides.securityBoundary: Strictly READ-ONLY — RECOMMENDS placement/purge, never moves or deletes (the mutation half is a separate owner-gated build). PROTECTED VETO (fail-closed): a protected/secret path is NEVER recommended for relocation or purge, even if misfiled (isProtectedPath is traversal-hardened). Deterministic: closed-set zone rules, sorted output, no RNG.
guides.whenToUse: Deciding where a generated artifact canonically belongs, finding misfiled files, or scoring stale purge candidates — to produce a report the OWNER acts on. Never to actually move/delete (that is owner-gated).
gotchas: READ-ONLY by contract — it recommends; the actual relocate/purge is a separate owner-gated mutation half, not here.
Protected/secret paths are NEVER recommended for move or purge, even when misfiled (fail-closed veto).
Zone classification is a CLOSED ordered ruleset (ZONE_RULES) — an artifact matching no rule gets the default zone, not an error.

guides.purpose: The LLM-WIELDED decoder instrument: translate text → a deterministic math object. NOT an ingress pre-processor that mutates input before the LLM — it is an INSTRUMENT the LLM calls directly: decode('<text>') returns a structured math representation (tokens, numerology channels, dimensional reading, feature surface) the LLM then reasons over. The control inverts — the model wields the decode engine.

exports.name: decode
exports.outputs: { tokens, numerology (gematria hash / digital-root mod-9 / harmonic signature), dimension, features, advisory_only } — a deterministic math object for the same text

guides.securityBoundary: Pure / read-only and advisory_only — computes a math object from text; persists nothing, touches no protected paths. Deterministic + embedding-free: same text → same object. Reuses the shipped channels (yuri-jaccard tokenize, nexus-numerology, the Foundry dimension classifier).
guides.whenToUse: When the model wants a deterministic structural reading of a piece of text (token surface, numerology channels, dimensional classification) to reason over — e.g. decoding a brain dump's surface features into a stable object.
gotchas: It is an INSTRUMENT the LLM calls, NOT an ingress mutator — it never rewrites the input before the model sees it.
Deterministic + embedding-free: identical text yields an identical object (no RNG, no clock) — good for caching/equality.
Output is advisory_only — a decoded reading is structure to reason over, not a verified claim.

newNode.label: YURI Nerve (nervous-system spine + afferent digest)
newNode.triggeredBy: import/CLI + wired into .claude/hooks/brain-inject.js — recordEvent captures a detected event under ONE id; organStateDigest surfaces the compact open-work heartbeat the brain wakes with each turn
newNode.description: The NERVOUS SYSTEM spine + afferent nerve. SPINE (one build, not three): a detected event is captured ONCE, gets ONE deterministic id (FNV-1a content hash, no clock), and is threaded across organs under that id — it becomes an OpenProcess-shaped entry (STATE/mass) AND carries a memory link (MEANING), cross-linked not duplicated. Closes three holes at once: auto-tracking, the memory↔task link, and durability (on disk the moment detected — the failure that lost the red-team findings). AFFERENT: organStateDigest() surfaces a COMPACT top-N organ-state the brain wakes with. Append-only store at _SYSTEM/state/nerve-events.jsonl; a later record for an id supersedes (reads as current state).

guides.purpose: The nervous-system spine + afferent nerve. A detected event is captured ONCE under ONE deterministic id and threaded across organs: it becomes an OpenProcess-shaped entry (STATE) carrying a memory link (MEANING), cross-linked not duplicated. organStateDigest() is the compact open-work heartbeat the brain wakes with each turn. Closes auto-tracking, the memory↔task link, and the durability hole in one spine.

exports.name: NERVE_KINDS
exports.outputs: ['task','decision','fix','finding','idea','correction','build','handoff']

exports.name: mintEventId
exports.outputs: a deterministic id 'nerve.<kind>.<fnv1a(title+content)>' — same input → same id (idempotent)

exports.name: recordEvent
exports.inputs: an event { kind, title, state, weight, evidence, refs, memoryLink, nextCandidateAction, closureCondition, stamp } + optional { store }
exports.outputs: { id, entry } — appends one JSONL line to the nerve store (mkdir-safe)

exports.name: loadEvents
exports.outputs: current events (de-duped by id: a later record supersedes; malformed lines skipped)

exports.name: closeEvent
exports.inputs: an event id + optional { kind, title, memoryLink, stamp }
exports.outputs: { ok, id, entry } — records a state:'closed' transition under the same id, carrying the memory link forward

exports.name: organStateDigest
exports.outputs: { op:'organ_state_digest', openCount, closedCount, top:[{id,type,title,mass,next}], advisory_only } — the afferent heartbeat

guides.securityBoundary: MUTATING but bounded: appends to the nerve store (_SYSTEM/state/nerve-events.jsonl, append-only JSONL, mkdir-safe) — never deletes or rewrites; a state transition is a NEW superseding record. No protected-path access. Deterministic: stable content-hash ids, caller-stamped time (no clock here). organStateDigest is advisory_only.
guides.whenToUse: Durably capturing a detected event (task/decision/fix/finding/idea/correction/build/handoff) the moment it occurs so it survives compaction; closing an event; or pulling the compact open-work digest the brain wakes with (`yuri-nerve.mjs digest`). The continuity spine — record-on-detect, recall-on-wake.
gotchas: Ids are content-hashed (FNV-1a) so re-detecting the same event is idempotent — it supersedes, it does not duplicate.
No clock inside: the caller supplies stamp; without it, time-ordering relies on append order only.
The store is append-only and reads via de-dup-by-id — a later line for an id is the current state (closeEvent works this way).
Only `digest` is wired as a CLI subcommand; recordEvent/closeEvent are the import surface (callers stamp + supply the event).
